[[Linda Nosková]] defeated [[Karolína Muchová]] in the final, 6–2, 5–7, 6–3 to win the ladies' singles tennis title at the [[2026 Wimbledon Championships]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/tennis/noskova-beats-muchova-win-wimbledon-womens-singles-title-2026-07-11/|title=Noskova beats Muchova to win Wimbledon women's singles title|publisher=Reuters|date=11 July 2026|accessdate=11 July 2026}}</ref> She [[List of Grand Slam related tennis records#Won a title after saving match points|saved a match point]] (in the third round against [[Sorana Cîrstea]]) en route to her first [[Grand Slam (tennis)#Tournaments|major]] title and third career [[WTA Tour]] title overall.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rfi.fr/en/sports/20260711-noskova-survives-tearful-meltdown-to-win-first-wimbledon-title|title=Noskova survives tearful meltdown to win first Wimbledon title|publisher=Radio France Internationale|date=11 July 2026|accessdate=11 July 2026}}</ref> Aged 21 years and 236 days old, Nosková was the youngest [[Wimbledon Championships|Wimbledon]] champion since [[Petra Kvitová]] in [[2011 Wimbledon Championships – Women's singles|2011]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4533700/at-21-linda-noskova-caps-brilliant-fortnight-to-become-youngest-wimbledon-champion-in-15-years-defeats-karolina-muchova|title=At 21, Noskova caps a brilliant fortnight to become youngest Wimbledon champion in 15 years|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|date=11 July 2026|accessdate=11 July 2026}}</ref> The [[Czech Republic]] became the sixth country in the Open Era to have [[List of Grand Slam women's singles finals#All-countrywomen finals (Open Era)|two countrywomen]] contest a major singles final.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Chiu |first1=Nigel |title=Wimbledon 2026: Karolina Muchova beats Coco Gauff after epic tie-break to set up all-Czech final against Linda Noskova |url=https://www.skysports.com/tennis/news/12110/13562014/wimbledon-2026-karolina-muchova-beats-coco-gauff-after-epic-tie-break-to-set-up-all-czech-final-against-linda-noskova |website=Sky Sports |access-date=9 July 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

[[Iga Świątek]] was the defending champion,<ref>{{cite web|last=Ostlere|first=Lawrence|title=How Amanda Anisimova’s Wimbledon nightmare unfolded in 57-minute onslaught by Iga Swiatek|website=The Independent|date=12 July 2025|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/tennis/iga-swiatek-amanda-anisimova-wimbledon-2025-final-result-tennis-b2787916.html|access-date=4 June 2026}}</ref> but lost in the third round to [[Alexandra Eala]]. Eala became the first Filipina player in the [[History of tennis#Open Era|Open Era]] to reach the third and fourth rounds of a major.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4530668/eala-dethrones-swiatek-at-wimbledon-to-make-new-history-for-the-philippines |title= Eala dethrones Swiatek at Wimbledon to make new history for the Philippines|website=WTAtennis|date=4 July 2026}} </ref> The defeat of [[Barbora Krejčíková]] in the fourth round guaranteed a first-time Wimbledon champion for the ninth consecutive edition.

[[Aryna Sabalenka]] retained the [[List of WTA number 1 ranked singles tennis players|world No. 1]] singles ranking after [[Elena Rybakina]] lost in the third round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tennisworldusa.org/tennis/news/WTA_Tennis/167802/aryna-sabalenka-benefits-from-elena-rybakina-s-3r-wimbledon-exit-no-1-spot-is-safe/|title=Aryna Sabalenka benefits from Elena Rybakina's 3R Wimbledon exit, No. 1 spot is safe|publisher=Tennis World USA|date=4 July 2026|accessdate=10 July 2026}}</ref> Sabalenka's fourth-round defeat to [[Naomi Osaka]] marked the first time she failed to reach the quarterfinals of a major since the [[2022 French Open – Women's singles|2022 French Open]], and her first straight-sets defeat at a major since the [[2020 US Open – Women's singles|2020 US Open]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Wimbledon 2026: Osaka beats top seed Sabalenka, Djokovic through, Gauff and Sinner in action on day seven |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2026/jul/05/wimbledon-2026-djokovic-sabalenka-sinner-and-gauff-in-action-on-day-seven-live |website=The Guardian |publisher=The Guardian |access-date=5 July 2026}}</ref>

This tournament marked the singles return of former world No. 1 and 23-time major champion [[Serena Williams]], who last played at the [[2022 US Open – Women's singles|2022 US Open]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wimbledon.com/en_GB/news/serena-williams-will-compete-in-the-2026-ladies--singles-at-wimb|title=Serena Williams enters 2026 ladies' singles as a wild card|website=The Championships, Wimbledon|date=21 June 2026|access-date=21 June 2026}}</ref> She lost in the first round to [[Maya Joint]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/articles/c802jk8rz44o|title=Williams falls just short on Wimbledon singles return|date=30 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=30 June 2026}}</ref> [[Maja Chwalińska]] was the third player in the Open Era to be seeded at a major while also being entered as a wildcard, following [[Martina Hingis]] at the [[2002 US Open – Women's singles|2002 US Open]] and [[Patty Schnyder]] at the [[2004 Wimbledon Championships – Women's singles|2004 Wimbledon Championships]].<ref>{{cite web |title= Only 3rd in Open Era: Maja Chwalinska to Be Both Wild-Card and Seed at Wimbledon|website=Tennis Temple|date=18 June 2026 |url= https://en.tennistemple.com/actu/only-3rd-in-open-era-maja-chwalinska-to-be-both/Y3wI |access-date=18 June 2026}}</ref> [[Lina Gjorcheska]] became the first player from [[North Macedonia]] to compete in a major main draw.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4526915/andreescu-takes-detour-back-to-wimbledon-gjorcheska-makes-national-history |website=WTATennis|title=Andreescu takes detour back to Wimbledon; Gjorcheska makes national history|date=25 June 2026}}</ref>
